value.body: An urban planner works out how land in a city or region is to be used: where housing, roads, parks, industry and services go, and how they connect. Employers include development authorities, municipal bodies, planning and infrastructure consultancies, and research organisations. A typical day mixes surveys and data work, GIS mapping, drafting plan documents and meetings with officials.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Plan, or an M.Plan after B.Arch / B.Tech Civil

items.label: Common tools
items.value: QGIS / ArcGIS, AutoCAD, Excel, survey forms

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join planning or infrastructure consultancies as planning associates on government projects such as master plans and smart-city work. Government planning posts are filled through state PSCs or development authorities, and some ask for ITPI membership or an M.Plan.

value.title: At a glance
items: Much consultancy work depends on government project cycles.
Many planners specialise later in transport, housing or environmental planning.
Next roles: senior planner, project manager, town planning officer.
